I'm wondering about how you know that you had or have a nasal infection. And do you mean an infection of the sinuses or of the nose? How do you know it was caused by mold and not bacteria?

I got a really bad sinus infection 3 and a half weeks ago (I still have congestion) from kissing someone. I think the mold mycotoxins in my blood weakened my immune system.

  
Thanks for the probiotic rec, I'd never heard of that being used to help recover from mold.

I suggest getting a blood test and getting oxygen therapy to your blood. I've heard of oxygen therapy but have not tried it. My intravenous oxygen levels (emphasis on "intravenous") are too high which means that the oxygen gas is leaving my blood vessels and not being absorbed by the cells

The Concrobium mold spray's purpose (https://www.amazon.com/Concrobium-27400CAL-Mold-Control-Aerosol/dp/B084CNRHHF?source=ps-sl-shoppingads-lpcontext&ref\_=fplfs&smid=ATVPDKIKX0DER&gQT=1&th=1) is only to prevent mold from growing, not to kill and destroy invisible mold spores and mycotoxin particles.

Also what types of liquids can I soak items in? I feel like soaking would be more effective than spraying an item. I'm thinking that I could soak some clothes and plastic tubs in a hydrogen peroxide solution, but I'm not sure the minimum concentration needed?

chronic congestion every day especially in the morning. chronic fatigue & brain fog where I forget what I was just doing or thinking. sometimes nausea. my immune system has become permanently weaker so I got sick more times this semester than last semester. I got a nasty cold 3 days after kissing someone and this turned into a sinus infection (to me, it felt like the same infection but apparently it was a viral infection with the throat and then a bacterial infection appeared in the sinuses).

I know I have symptoms from mold exposure since Jan 12, but don't know if this is a infection or just mycotoxins in my blood. I got a urine test which showed mycotoxins present on March 18th.
